examples.ko: 그 사람이 우리를 이간질해서 사이가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: That person set us against each other, and our relationship soured.

examples.ko: 친구들을 이간질하는 사람과는 멀리하세요.
examples.en: Stay away from people who turn friends against each other.

examples.ko: 거짓말로 부부를 이간질하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not drive a couple apart with lies.

examples.ko: 누가 이간질했는지 꼭 알아내고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to find out who stirred up the trouble.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 이간질하고 다니는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone going around sowing discord behind our backs.

examples.ko: 이간질하려는 말에 흔들리지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't be shaken by words meant to split you up.

explain: 남의 사이를 일부러 나쁘게 만드는 일이에요. '~을/를 이간질하다', '두 사람을 이간질하다'로 써요. 같은 뜻의 '이간하다'는 주로 글에서 보여요.

phrases.en: Please don't try to come between us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형 존댓말로, 상대에게 그만하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative command telling someone to stop.

phrases.en: You shouldn't trust people who sow discord.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 꾸며 주는 관형형으로 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing a type of person.

phrases.en: Someone drove a wedge between the two of them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사이를'과 함께 쓰면 누구 사이인지 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 사이를, it is clear whose relationship is affected.

explain_en: It means deliberately making a relationship between others go bad, used as '~을/를 이간질하다' or '두 사람을 이간질하다'. The same-meaning '이간하다' appears mostly in writing.

en: to sneer; to jeer; to make sarcastic remarks

examples.ko: 그 애는 내 실수를 보고 이죽거렸어요.
examples.en: He sneered when he saw my mistake.

examples.ko: 옆에서 이죽거리지 말고 도와줘요.
examples.en: Stop sneering from the side and help me.

examples.ko: 그가 이죽거리는 말투가 정말 얄미워요.
examples.en: His sneering way of talking is really annoying.

examples.ko: 친구가 이죽거려서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My friend made snide remarks, and it made me angry.

examples.ko: 이죽거리며 놀리는 사람은 피하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to avoid people who tease with sneers.

examples.ko: 왜 내 얘기만 나오면 자꾸 이죽거려요?
examples.en: Why do you keep making snide remarks whenever I come up?

explain: 비꼬듯이 얄밉게 말하거나 비웃는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 말인 '빈정거리다'도 있고, '이죽대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. 듣는 사람이 기분 나쁜 부정적인 상황에서 써요.

phrases.en: I heard someone sneering behind me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이죽거리다'와 같은 뜻으로, 조금 더 짧게 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 이죽거리다 in a shorter form.

phrases.en: I fought with my friend because of his sneering tone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 말하는 방식이 얄밉다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's irritating, mocking way of speaking.

phrases.en: Don't be sarcastic, just say it honestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비꼬며 말하는 비슷한 동사로, 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar verb for sarcasm, more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: It describes talking in a mocking, annoying way, or sneering at someone. '빈정거리다' is a similar word, and '이죽대다' means the same. It is used in negative situations where the listener feels bad.

en: to burst out; to be convulsed; to cringe in fright

examples.ko: 아기가 놀라서 자지러지며 울었어요.
examples.en: The baby was startled and burst into a shrieking cry.

examples.ko: 친구의 농담에 모두가 자지러지게 웃었어요.
examples.en: Everyone burst into fits of laughter at my friend's joke.

examples.ko: 천둥소리에 강아지가 깜짝 놀라 자지러졌어요.
examples.en: The puppy jumped in fright at the thunder.

examples.ko: 자지러지는 웃음소리가 복도까지 들렸어요.
examples.en: The roaring laughter could be heard all the way down the hall.

examples.ko: 주사를 맞자 아이가 자지러져서 달래느라 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The child shrieked at the shot, and it was hard to calm him.

examples.ko: 영화가 너무 웃겨서 자지러질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The movie was so funny that I nearly died laughing.

explain: 소리가 갑자기 높고 크게 터져 나오는 모습에 써요. 주로 '자지러지게 울다, 웃다'로 말하고, 깜짝 놀라 몸이 움츠러드는 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The baby was startled and cried shrilly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 울음소리가 갑자기 높고 크게 터져 나올 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for crying that suddenly bursts out high and loud.

phrases.en: Everyone burst out laughing at my friend's joke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨이 넘어갈 만큼 크게 웃는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes laughing so hard one almost loses breath.
phrases.en_equiv: to burst into shrieks of laughter

phrases.en: I saw a bug and shrank back in shock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몹시 놀라서 몸이 움츠러드는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shrinking back in great fright.

explain_en: Shriek or convulse — mostly babies crying or people laughing hard. It describes a sound bursting out suddenly and loudly. It mostly appears as '자지러지게 울다/웃다' (to shriek or burst into laughter), and can also be used for flinching in fright.

t90.ax: The puppy jumped in fright at the thunder.

en: to chat; to have a chat; to gab

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 친구와 잡담하다가 선생님께 혼났어요.
examples.en: I got scolded by the teacher for chatting with a friend in class.

examples.ko: 우리는 커피를 마시며 한 시간 동안 잡담했어요.
examples.en: We chatted over coffee for an hour.

examples.ko: 회의 전에 동료들과 잠깐 잡담해요.
examples.en: I make small talk with my colleagues for a bit before meetings.

examples.ko: 일할 때 너무 많이 잡담하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you chat too much while working, you can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 그냥 잡담하러 왔어요.
examples.en: I just came to chat.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터에서 이웃과 잡담하는 게 어색해요.
examples.en: Making small talk with a neighbor in the elevator feels awkward.

explain: '이야기하다'보다 가볍고 중요하지 않은 얘기를 편하게 나눌 때 써요. '수다 떨다'는 즐겁고 길게 떠드는 느낌이고, 잡담은 별 내용 없는 일상 이야기라 수업이나 회의에서는 부정적으로 들릴 수 있어요. 명사로 '잡담을 하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I chat with my friends during the break.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡담하다'와 같은 뜻으로, 명사 뒤에 '을 하다'를 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, formed by adding 을 하다 to the noun.

phrases.en: I chatted away with a friend at a cafe on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡담보다 즐겁고 길게 이야기하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more cheerful and longer than 잡담.

phrases.en: Please don't chat during the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이나 회의에서 조용히 하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask people to be quiet in class or meetings.

explain_en: Idle, aimless chatter; casual spoken, can sound trivial. It is lighter than '이야기하다', used for casually trading unimportant talk. '수다 떨다' feels like chatting happily at length, while 잡담하다 is content-free everyday talk that can sound negative in class or at meetings. You can also say it as a noun phrase, '잡담을 하다'.

en: to interfere; to intervene; to step in

examples.ko: 남의 일에 너무 참견하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't butt into other people's business so much.

examples.ko: 엄마가 제 옷차림까지 참견해서 조금 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's a bit hard because my mom even interferes with what I wear.

examples.ko: 옆에서 자꾸 참견하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you keep butting in beside me, I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 제가 참견할 일은 아니지만 걱정이 돼서요.
examples.en: It's not my place to interfere, but I'm worried.

examples.ko: 동생은 언니 일에 참견하기를 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling likes to meddle in her older sister's affairs.

examples.ko: 누가 참견해도 저는 제 길을 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Even if someone interferes, I'll go my own way.

explain: '간섭하다'와 비슷하지만 '참견하다'는 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰고, 달갑지 않게 끼어드는 느낌이 있어요. '남의 일에 참견하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 사람에게는 '오지랖이 넓다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: My friend said, "Don't butt into my business."
phrases.nuance_ko: 반말 금지 표현이라서 친한 사이에서 쓰고, 윗사람에게는 '참견하지 마세요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a casual-speech prohibition for close friends. To someone older, say 참견하지 마세요.

phrases.example: 부모님이 제 일에 일일이 참견해서 답답해요.
phrases.en: My parents interfere in every little thing I do, and it feels stifling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 일까지 하나하나 끼어드는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone stepping in on every small matter.
phrases.en_equiv: to meddle in every little thing

phrases.en: My coworker keeps interfering in my work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '참견하다'보다 조금 딱딱하고, 규칙이나 일에 끼어들 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but a bit more formal than 참견하다. It's also used for stepping into rules or work.

explain_en: Spoken — nosy remarks on others' business; negative. It is similar to '간섭하다' (to interfere), but '참견하다' is more common in everyday talk and carries a feeling of unwelcome butting in. It is often used with the particle '에', as in '남의 일에 참견하다'. For a person like this, Koreans also say '오지랖이 넓다'.

t90.ax: Even if someone interferes, I'll go my own way.

en: to pose as; to act as if one were

examples.ko: 그 사람은 의사처럼 행세하며 사람들을 속였어요.
examples.en: That person posed as a doctor and deceived people.

examples.ko: 그는 부자인 것처럼 행세하고 다녀요.
examples.en: He goes around acting as if he's rich.

examples.ko: 친구가 다 아는 척 행세해서 다들 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend acted like he knew everything, and everyone laughed.

examples.ko: 높은 사람처럼 행세하는 태도가 마음에 안 들어요.
examples.en: I don't like the attitude of acting like a big shot.

examples.ko: 사기꾼은 경찰로 행세하며 전화를 걸어요.
examples.en: Scammers call people pretending to be police officers.

examples.ko: 아무리 잘난 척 행세해도 실력은 금방 드러나요.
examples.en: No matter how much you act superior, your real skill soon shows.

explain: 실제와 다르게 어떤 신분이나 지위인 것처럼 굴 때 써요. '~처럼/~로 행세하다' 형태가 많고, 대부분 좋지 않은 느낌이에요. 단순히 '~인 척하다'보다 사회적 지위나 신분을 내세우는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 그는 선생님 행세를 하며 돈을 요구했어요.
phrases.en: He posed as a teacher and demanded money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '행세'를 써서 어떤 신분인 것처럼 굴 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 행세 to say someone acts as if they hold a certain status.

phrases.en: You shouldn't act like the owner when you're a guest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 위치가 아닌데 높은 자리인 척 굴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts as if they hold a position that isn't theirs.

phrases.en: Don't pass yourself off as an expert when you know nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명령형 부정으로, 그렇게 굴지 말라고 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to warn someone not to put on such an act.

explain_en: Acting like a certain kind of person, often putting on airs. It is used when someone acts as if they have a certain status or position that is not really theirs. It often appears as '~처럼/~로 행세하다' and usually has a negative feel. Compared with plain '~인 척하다', it leans more toward putting on a social status or identity.

t90.ax: He goes around acting as if he's rich.

examples.ko: 시장에서 강매를 당할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost got pressured into buying something at the market.

examples.ko: 인터넷에는 강매 피해 후기가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many reviews online from people who were victims of forced sales.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 강매로 신고를 당했대요.
examples.en: I heard that store was reported for forced selling.

examples.ko: 강매는 소비자의 권리를 해치는 일이에요.
examples.en: Forced selling harms consumers' rights.

examples.ko: 강매에 속지 않으려면 계약서를 꼼꼼히 보세요.
examples.en: To avoid being tricked by pushy sales, read the contract carefully.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 가이드가 물건 강매를 해서 불쾌했어요.
examples.en: During the trip, the guide pushed us to buy things, and it was unpleasant.

explain: 사고 싶지 않은 사람에게 물건을 억지로 사게 하는 일을 말해요. 피해를 본 사람 입장에서는 '강매를 당하다'라고 말하고, 소비자 보호나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서 가볍게는 '억지로 팔다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I was forced to buy something on the street, so I felt bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural expression from the buyer's point of view.

phrases.en: Damage from coercive selling among the elderly is increasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 소비자 이야기에서 많이 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in news and consumer topics.

phrases.en: Coercive selling is prohibited by law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 법을 말할 때 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression used when talking about rules or law.

explain_en: Negative: pressuring someone to buy, as in tourist traps. It means making someone buy something they don't want to buy. From the victim's side it is '강매를 당하다', and it often appears in consumer-protection topics and news. In casual speech people might also say '억지로 팔다'.

examples.ko: 길에서 노점상 아주머니께 붕어빵을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought fish-shaped pastries from a street vendor lady.

examples.ko: 퇴근길에 노점상에서 과일을 사 갔어요.
examples.en: On my way home from work I bought fruit from a street stall.

examples.ko: 시장 앞 노점상들이 비가 오면 장사를 일찍 접어요.
examples.en: The street vendors in front of the market close early when it rains.

examples.ko: 노점상 할아버지가 덤으로 귤을 더 주셨어요.
examples.en: The old street vendor gave me extra tangerines for free.

examples.ko: 구청이 노점상 단속을 시작했다고 해요.
examples.en: I heard the district office has started cracking down on street vendors.

examples.ko: 명동에는 노점상이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: There are so many street vendors in Myeongdong.

explain: 길가에 자리를 잡고 물건을 파는 가게나 그 일을 하는 사람을 가리켜요. '포장마차'는 천막을 친 간이 가게를 말해서, 노점상 중 한 종류예요. 뉴스에서는 '노점상 단속'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The news talked about a crackdown on street vendors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often used in the news.

phrases.en: I bought hotteok at a stall across the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노점'은 길가의 가게를 말하고, 일상 대화에서 짧게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '노점' means a roadside stall and is a short form used in daily talk.
phrases.en_equiv: to buy at a street stall

phrases.en: After work, I ate fish cake at a street food tent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천막을 친 간이 가게로, 노점상 가운데 한 종류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tent-style stall, one kind of street vendor.

explain_en: It refers to a roadside stall or the person who runs one. A '포장마차' is a tent-covered stall, so it is one kind of street vendor. News often uses it in phrases like '노점상 단속' (street vendor crackdown).

examples.ko: 그 사람은 돈놀이로 큰돈을 벌었대요.
examples.en: I heard that person made a fortune lending money.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 돈놀이 같은 건 절대 안 하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather never did anything like moneylending.

examples.ko: 이웃 아줌마가 몰래 돈놀이를 한다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that our neighbor secretly lends money for interest.

examples.ko: 돈놀이하는 사람에게 돈을 빌리면 이자가 무서워요.
examples.en: If you borrow from a moneylender, the interest is frightening.

examples.ko: 월급만으로 부족해서 돈놀이를 시작했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he started lending money because his salary wasn't enough.

examples.ko: 돈놀이에 빠지면 사람이 변한다고들 해요.
examples.en: People say that once you get into moneylending, you change.

explain: 이자를 받으려고 돈을 빌려주는 일인데, 어딘가 탐탁지 않게 보는 어감이 있어요. 은행 일이나 정식 대출을 말할 때는 '대출', '대부'처럼 중립적인 말을 써요. '돈놀이하다'처럼 동사로도 말해요.

phrases.en: I heard he bought a house by lending money at interest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 동사로 바꾼 말이고 말투가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of the noun, and it sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: If you borrow from a loan shark, the interest is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈놀이를 직업처럼 하는 사람을 낮추어 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat derogatory term for someone who makes a living lending money.

phrases.en: That person makes a living from moneylending.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈놀이가 생계 수단이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means moneylending is how the person earns a living.

explain_en: It means lending money to earn interest, with a slightly disapproving tone. For banks or formal loans, people use neutral words like '대출' or '대부'. It also works as a verb: '돈놀이하다'.

en: to be exhausted; to run out; to be sold out

examples.ko: 인기 있는 빵은 오전에 벌써 동나요.
examples.en: The popular bread has already run out by the morning.

examples.ko: 마스크가 동나서 약국을 여러 군데 돌았어요.
examples.en: Masks were sold out, so I went around to several pharmacies.

examples.ko: 용돈이 벌써 동났어요.
examples.en: My allowance has already run out.

examples.ko: 콘서트 표가 순식간에 동났대요.
examples.en: I heard the concert tickets sold out in an instant.

examples.ko: 재료가 동나면 일찍 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: When the ingredients run out, we close early.

examples.ko: 물건이 다 동날 때까지 세일을 해요.
examples.en: They have the sale until everything is gone.

explain: '떨어지다'는 조금 모자라게 된 때도 쓰지만, '동나다'는 가게의 물건이나 재고가 하나도 남지 않았을 때 잘 써요. '표가 동나다', '재료가 동나다'처럼 팔리거나 써서 바닥난 경우에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 점심때가 되기 전에 도시락이 다 동났어요.
phrases.en: The lunch boxes were all sold out before lunchtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 다 없어졌다는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, meaning it has already run out.

phrases.en: Popular items run out of stock quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게의 물건이 남지 않았을 때 잘 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when a store's goods are gone.

phrases.en: The concert tickets sold out in two days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 많이 사서 더 살 수 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means so many people bought them that none are left.

explain_en: Stock or goods run out; spoken, shops and food. '떨어지다' can also be used when something is merely running short, but '동나다' fits stock that has completely run out, such as goods in a shop. It suits things that sold out or got used up, as in '표가 동나다' or '재료가 동나다'.

t90.ax: My allowance has already run out.

examples.ko: 사채를 쓰면 이자가 너무 높아서 위험해요.
examples.en: Using a private loan is risky because the interest is so high.

examples.ko: 가게가 어려워지자 사장님이 사채에 손을 댔어요.
examples.en: When the shop got into trouble, the owner turned to private loans.

examples.ko: 사채로 빌린 돈을 갚느라 고생했어요.
examples.en: I had a hard time paying back the money I borrowed from a loan shark.

examples.ko: 은행 대출이 안 돼도 사채는 쓰지 말라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: They told me not to use private lenders even if I can't get a bank loan.

examples.ko: 사채 빚이 눈덩이처럼 불어났어요.
examples.en: The debt to the private lender snowballed.

examples.ko: 사채업자를 조심하라는 경고 문자를 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a warning text telling me to watch out for loan sharks.

explain: 은행이 아니라 개인이나 업체가 빌려주는 돈을 말하고, 이자가 높은 경우가 많아서 나쁜 느낌으로 자주 써요. '사채업자', '사채 빚'처럼 많이 말해요. 경제 뉴스에서는 회사가 발행하는 채권을 뜻하는 '사채'(社債)도 있어서 문맥을 봐야 해요.

phrases.example: 급해서 사채를 썼다가 빚이 크게 늘었어요.
phrases.en: I used a private loan in a hurry and my debt grew a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사채로 돈을 빌린다는 뜻으로 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say borrowing money from a private lender.

phrases.en: A loan shark called every day, so I was scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사채를 빌려주는 사람을 말하고 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the lender and carries a negative feeling.

phrases.example: 사채 빚을 갚느라 몇 년 동안 고생했어요.
phrases.en: I struggled for years to pay off my private loan debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사채로 생긴 빚이 부담스럽다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the burdensome debt that came from such a loan.

explain_en: It means money lent by individuals or businesses rather than banks, often at high interest, so it usually has a negative tone. Common forms are '사채업자' and '사채 빚'. In economic news, '사채' (社債) can also mean a corporate bond, so check the context.

examples.ko: 사채업자에게 돈을 빌렸다가 이자 때문에 고생했어요.
examples.en: He borrowed money from a loan shark and suffered because of the interest.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 사채업자의 높은 이자가 문제라고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said the high interest of private lenders is a problem.

examples.ko: 사채업자한테 빌리면 안 된다고 부모님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents told me never to borrow from a private moneylender.

examples.ko: 친구가 사채업자 때문에 힘들어해서 같이 상담을 받으러 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend was struggling because of a private lender, so we went for counseling together.

examples.ko: 은행 대신 사채업자를 찾는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: More people are turning to private lenders instead of banks.

examples.ko: 사채업자가 전화를 자꾸 해서 불안해요.
examples.en: The private lender keeps calling, so I feel anxious.

explain: 은행 같은 정식 금융기관이 아닌 개인에게 돈을 빌려주는 사람을 말하고, 높은 이자 때문에 좋지 않은 느낌이 있어요. '사채를 쓰다'와 함께 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 법에 따라 등록한 곳은 보통 '대부업체'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I was in a hurry and took a private loan, and my debt grew.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사채'는 개인에게 빌린 돈이고, 이 표현은 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 사채 is money borrowed from private lenders, and this phrase often appears in the news.

phrases.en: I heard he is being chased by loan sharks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 갚지 못해 힘든 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a difficult situation where someone cannot repay money.
phrases.en_equiv: to be chased by a moneylender

phrases.en: Licensed lenders charge higher interest than banks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 따라 등록한 돈 빌려주는 곳을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The term for a registered lender that operates under the law.

explain_en: It refers to a person who lends money outside regular financial institutions, and it carries a negative image because of high interest. It often appears in the news with '사채를 쓰다' (to take a private loan). Registered lenders are usually called '대부업체'.

examples.ko: 신병들은 처음엔 군기 때문에 크게 긴장해요.
examples.en: New recruits are very tense at first because of the discipline.

examples.ko: 선배가 후배의 군기를 잡는 문화는 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: The culture of seniors putting juniors in line is a problem.

examples.ko: 요즘 군대의 군기는 예전보다 많이 부드러워졌어요.
examples.en: Discipline in the military these days has become much softer than before.

examples.ko: 군기도 좋고 분위기도 좋은 부대로 소문났어요.
examples.en: It has a reputation as a unit with good discipline and a good atmosphere.

examples.ko: 새로 온 팀장님은 군기가 세다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: People say the new team leader is strict about discipline.

examples.ko: 군기로 사람을 누르려는 방식은 이제 통하지 않아요.
examples.en: Trying to control people through strict discipline doesn't work anymore.

explain: 원래 군대의 규율이지만, 동아리나 회사처럼 분위기가 엄격하고 위아래가 분명한 곳에도 비유로 써요. '군기가 세다', '군기가 빠지다', '군기를 잡다'처럼 자주 말해요. 어느 정도 부정적인 느낌으로 들릴 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 선배들이 신입생 군기를 잡는다고 소문이 났어요.
phrases.en: There's a rumor that the seniors are putting the freshmen in line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대와 상관없이 후배나 신입을 엄하게 다뤄서 질서를 세운다는 뜻이에요. 보통 부정적으로 쓰고, 가벼운 농담으로도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Regardless of the military, it means treating juniors or newcomers harshly to enforce order. It is usually negative, though it can also be said jokingly.
phrases.en_equiv: put someone in line / lay down the law

explain_en: It originally means discipline in the military, but it is also used figuratively for places like clubs or companies where the atmosphere is strict and the hierarchy is clear. Common phrases are '군기가 세다', '군기가 빠지다' and '군기를 잡다'. It often sounds somewhat negative.

examples.ko: 발표 전날 밤에 자료를 급조했어요.
examples.en: I threw the materials together the night before the presentation.

examples.ko: 급조한 계획이라 빈틈이 많아요.
examples.en: It's a hastily made plan, so it has many gaps.

examples.ko: 손님이 갑자기 와서 반찬을 급조해 냈어요.
examples.en: Guests came suddenly, so I whipped up some side dishes.

examples.ko: 이런 일은 급조하면 꼭 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you rush this kind of work, problems always come up.

examples.ko: 팀을 급조하지 말고 천천히 준비해요.
examples.en: Let's not put a team together in a rush; let's prepare slowly.

examples.ko: 급조할 시간이 없어서 있는 걸로 했어요.
examples.en: There was no time to improvise, so I used what I had.

explain: 서둘러 대충 만들었다는 느낌이 있어서 좋은 뜻으로는 잘 안 써요. '급조한 느낌이 나다'처럼 완성도가 떨어진다고 말할 때 자주 나와요. '임시로 만들다'보다 서두른 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: I had no time, so I threw the report together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거 해요체로, 서둘러 대충 만들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form meaning something was made hastily and roughly.

phrases.en: This poster looks like it was thrown together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완성도가 낮아 보일 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when something looks unpolished.

phrases.en: I put the materials together in a hurry, so there were many mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서둘러 만든 것이 이유가 되어 나쁜 결과가 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hasty work leads to a bad result.

explain_en: It carries a sense of making something quickly and roughly, so it is rarely positive. It often appears when saying something feels rushed, like '급조한 느낌이 나다'. It stresses the hurry more than '임시로 만들다' (to make temporarily).
